title: add-benchmark-lab-adaptive-batching-reporting-pipeline-v69
author: Maya Chen
body: Summary: Adds a reporting pipeline and supporting runners for the benchmark lab to capture adaptive-batching experiments (v69). Motivation: recent scheduler changes enabled adaptive-batching policies that vary batch size by workload characteristics; we need consistent profiling and a reporting pipeline to collect, normalize, and visualize results across model variants and hardware. This PR introduces new workload runners, instrumentation for adaptive batch metrics, an ETL that aggregates run-level traces into the benchmark datastore, and dashboards for per-run comparisons. Scope: - benchmark-lab/runners/adaptive_runner.py: new representative runner that exercises adaptive batching policies and records per-step batch-size, latency, token-throughput, and scheduling decisions. - benchmark-lab/profiling/baselines/adaptive_v69/: baseline configs + small corpus for regressions. - infra/reporting/pipelines/adaptive_v69_etl.py: Airflow DAG (as code) that pulls raw run artifacts, normalizes KV-cache warmup windows, computes steady-state and cold-start metrics, and writes summarized rows to BigQuery table benchmark_lab.adaptive_v69_summary. - observability/dashboards/adaptive_v69.json: Grafana dashboard panels for batch-size distribution, P50/P95 latencies, throughput, and regression alerts. - tests: unit tests for the ETL, integration smoke that runs a short adaptive runner via GH Actions. Changes are backward-compatible and opt-in via a new config flag `adaptive_reporting.enabled` defaulting to false for existing customers. Checklist: - [x] Add representative runner and baseline configs - [x] Implement ETL and unit tests - [x] Add dashboard and example queries - [x] Wire GH Actions smoke test for CI - [x] Add documentation section in benchmark-lab README Testing and validation: Local unit tests run in ~90s. Integration smoke runs in CI with a trimmed corpus and mock GCS to avoid external dependencies; CI initially failed the integration step due to a flaky fixture (timing), which was fixed by adding a deterministic seed and an explicit wait-for-metrics step. We validated results on a small fleet (dedicated test cluster) and compared with previous non-adaptive baselines; differences are within expected variance and are surfaced in the dashboard. Rollout plan: feature gated behind `adaptive_reporting.enabled`; will enable for internal benchmark team for 2 weeks, then opt into public pipeline. Related: ENG-1634 (adaptive batching feature), ENG-1702 (benchmark reporting improvements). Release notes: Adds adaptive-batching benchmark runners and reporting pipeline (experimental opt-in).
commits: Add adaptive_runner implementation and basic config
Add ETL airflow DAG and normalization logic
Add dashboards and queries for adaptive_v69
Add unit tests and GH Actions smoke workflow
Fix flaky fixture by seeding RNG and adding wait-for-metrics step
review_comments: Arjun Patel: Please add a short doc blurb describing how we normalize KV-cache warmup windows - I want to be sure the steady-state calculation is comparable across model sizes.
Maya Chen (author): Added details in docs/benchmark-lab/AdaptiveBatching.md and included pseudocode for the warmup window detection algorithm.
Sofia Moreno: ETL writes to BigQuery directly from DAG; please add a retry/backoff and idempotency key to avoid duplicate rows on retry.
Maya Chen (author): ETL now writes to a staging table and uses a transactionless dedupe step keyed by run_id+variant. Added exponential backoff for remote calls.
Benji Liu: Small nits on variable names in adaptive_runner.py and a missing type hint in metrics_normalizer.py - otherwise LGTM.
Benji Liu: Approved after nits addressed (approval recorded).
release_notes: Experimental: Adds adaptive-batching benchmark runners (v69) and reporting pipeline. Opt-in via adaptive_reporting.enabled. Provides dashboards and ETL for aggregating adaptive run metrics.
notes: This PR was coordinated with the infra and observability teams; deployment to production ETL requires a scheduled window to update the BigQuery schema. No customer-facing API changes. Internal rollout only for first two weeks.
